# Jubilees Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham Dies; A Vision of the End of Days

---

**23:1** Abraham placed Jacob's two hands over his eyes and blessed God. Then he laid his own face against Jacob's face and kissed him, saying: "Blessed be the LORD God — blessed be his name forever and ever! He gave me Jacob — a pure son, a holy child. He is mine. May he be mine forever."

**23:2** "My son — I charge you: keep my commandments and walk the way of your father Abraham."

**23:3** Abraham died in the forty-third jubilee, in the sixth year of the seventh week. He had lived one hundred and seventy-five years, and he died in peace, having completed every year that was his.

**23:4** In the earliest ages, the ancient ones lived as long as nineteen jubilees. But after the Flood, human lifespans began to shrink — falling short of nineteen jubilees, then shorter still, aging faster, dying sooner. The cause was clear: the endless troubles that came from living wicked lives.

**23:5** The wicked have their days numbered against them — they are being cut short.

**23:6** Think of it this way: Noah was five hundred years old before Shem was born. Methuselah lived to nine hundred and sixty-nine.

**23:7** But the Most High was enraged at the Flood generation. Their hearts were rotten; their thoughts were corrupt every single day.

**23:8** After the Flood, lifespans kept dropping: from a hundred years to seventy, seventy to fifty, fifty to forty, forty to thirty-five, thirty-five to thirty, thirty to twenty-five, twenty-five to twenty.

**23:9** At twenty years old, old age will already be setting in. What's left of life will be lived in misery and grief.

**23:10** There won't be anyone who lives to feel satisfied with their years. Everyone will be like children — like teenagers who never grew up.

**23:11** Everything they do will be chaotic and malicious. They'll corrupt each other through their disgusting practices.

**23:12** A ten-year-old will say, "That eighty-year-old hasn't even lived yet — he's no older than a five-year-old."

**23:13** Everyone will be like a three-year-old child — clueless about which way to go.

**23:14** But then — in those same days — children will begin to study the law. They'll search out the commandments and find their way back to the path of righteousness.

**23:15** And when that happens, lifespans will begin to grow again. Human years will increase until they approach a thousand — more years than there ever were before.

**23:16** In those days, no one will grow old. No one will be worn out by age or plagued by evil. Everyone will be like young people and children, full of life for all their days.

**23:17** They'll live their whole lives in peace and joy. No adversary, no destroyer — just days of blessing and healing, one after another.

**23:18** In that time, the LORD will heal his servants. They'll stand up and see a great peace. They'll defeat their enemies. The righteous will look around and give thanks and overflow with joy — eternal joy — as they watch every curse and every judgment fall on those who persecuted them.

**23:19** Their bones will rest in the earth, but their spirits will be overjoyed. They'll know beyond doubt that the LORD is the one who brings justice — and who shows mercy to thousands and thousands who love him.

**23:20** Moses — write all of this down. It is written here, and it is recorded on the heavenly tablets: the divisions of the days, the law and the testimony, every event of every year, every week and jubilee, across all the ages of the world — until the day of the new creation, when heaven and earth and everything in them are made new, as fresh as the powers of heaven, as new as the first creatures of the earth — until the day when the LORD's sanctuary stands in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and every light in the sky is renewed for healing and peace and blessing, for all of God's chosen people in Israel, from that day on, for all the days of the earth.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Jubilees 23 is one of the most important apocalyptic passages in all Second Temple literature. The lifespan regression (v.8) is a remarkably systematic decline chart. The pivot in v.14 — when children return to the law — is the turning point of the whole eschatological vision. V.20 is a soaring climax linking Moses, the heavenly tablets, the new creation, and Zion.*
